angleRead.name: Simon Leary
angleRead.text: Simon Leary stands at the edge of the newsroom, staring out the window as the city fades into twilight. The A’s record looms large—127-35—a number that feels less like a statistic and more like a monument. He’s chasing the story of continuity, of how a team sustains itself even as roles shift beneath the surface. Benji Dillon’s move to the bullpen lingers in his mind, not as a disruption but as a quiet pivot within a structure that remains unshaken. Simon doesn’t need to know why the change was made; he’s after the metaphor, the way a single beam can shift without the whole edifice crumbling.
